name: context-broker
tagline: Answers big-file reads with an exact skeleton: 80 to 95% fewer tokens, no second model
summary: context-broker is a Claude Code hook that intercepts reads of large files and answers with the file's exact structure instead: imports, signatures and types as verbatim lines with real line numbers. It takes about a millisecond, runs entirely on your machine and sends nothing to another model. The agent then reads only the slices it needs by line range, so reading and editing a big file costs a fraction of a full read.

features: Verbatim source lines with real line numbers, so a skeleton can be incomplete but never wrong
Ranged reads always pass through, so the read-then-edit path needs no second full read
Fails open on any error, so the hook can never break a read
cb bench measures savings across your repo before you install, with no model calls
Also a CLI: skeleton, ranged read, log folding for noisy build output, and a running savings ledger
how_it_works: A PreToolUse hook catches Read calls on files over 350 lines; small files, binaries, images and ranged reads pass straight through.
The denial carries the answer: the file's skeleton, extracted by hand-rolled structural matchers for TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java and more.
The agent expands only the bodies it needs with ranged reads, which are never intercepted.
notes: No image or video assets in the repo. Suggested hero: render the README skeleton sample (numbered lines with 'a few lines elided' markers) and the benchmark table as a styled code block. Re-verified locally: ./test.sh prints 'all tests passed', and 'cb bench ../unclaude/src' printed '20 files over 350 lines · 124184 → 17660 tokens (86% saved) · scanned in 8.8ms' (usable as an extra data point if the builder wants a fresh run). No npm/PyPI package, no git tags or releases; .claude-plugin/plugin.json declares 0.1.0, so version is null (installed from main via the plugin marketplace). The 89% and per-file figures come from one production monorepo run quoted in the README (token counts use a chars/4 estimate, per the README). The README table that names another vendor's tool was deliberately not used. The README text contains en and em dashes; the quotes above were chosen to avoid them.
